key_insight: An LLM agent uses physics-based simulations to inverse-design fabrication recipes for target depth profiles of implanted ions or vacancies.
engineering_relevance: This approach could help translate desired spatial material structures into ion-processing recipes with minimal human input.
method: Specify a target depth profile of implanted ions or vacancies.
Let the agent select ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers.
Run and interpret ion–matter simulations, then iteratively refine the recipe to match the target.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based target-profile matching but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics, benchmark comparisons, or experimental fabrication validation.
watch_item: Practical fabrication performance depends on simulator fidelity and requires experimental validation of the proposed recipes.
paper_title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
